assessmentSummary.identity: From one declared support leg, project laterally through flight, land on the opposite leg, absorb to a stable terminal hold for the declared duration without an extra hop or free-foot touch, then reset fully before the next attempt.
currentCardFindings: The lateral-bound survivor already owns multiple exact lateral-bound-to-stick legacy sources, but its baseline fields do not explicitly declare the terminal hold, opposite-leg landing, or reset contract.
Archived source variants and aliases should not substitute for a selectable exact baseline.

This audit preserves opposite-leg lateral projection and terminal control while excluding same-leg lateral hops, continuous skater bounds, diagonal bounds, step-behind approaches, and reactive rebounds.
Five exact-title candidates returned current YouTube oEmbed metadata and iframe markup; movement, safety, accessibility, and demonstration approval remain human-review gates.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: both sides preserve lateral projection quiet whole-foot absorption alignment declared hold and full reset

athleteInstructions: Confirm both lateral landing zones are clear, dry, level, and wide enough for a safe miss.
Start on the declared takeoff leg with the opposite leg and arms ready to counterbalance.
Project directly sideways and land on the opposite leg; do not turn the rep into a same-leg line hop or diagonal cut.
Absorb through the foot, ankle, knee, and hip while keeping the pelvis and trunk controlled.
Hold for the declared duration without another hop or free-foot touch, then step out and reset fully.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain the stable lateral-bound slug but rename and constrain the selectable baseline to an opposite-leg lateral bound with terminal hold and full reset. Preserve generic and stick labels as aliases. Keep the card review-only until content, media, scoring, relationship, pilot, and card reviewers approve it.

currentCardSnapshot.description: The athlete bounds laterally from one leg to the other with a powerful push and stable landing.
